headline: TREASURY CRIME UNIT
dek: FinCEN, Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, says there was unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. It took some systems offline; the BSA E-Filing site remains operational.

graphic.title: FEDERAL SYSTEMS HIT · RECENTLY REPORTED

items.name: FINCEN
items.label: Treasury crime unit
items.text: Limited subset of systems accessed. Some systems taken offline.

items.name: CIA / ODNI
items.label: Unclassified intel-analysis system
items.text: Resolved, a person familiar said. Classified systems unaffected.

items.name: FBI NCIC
items.label: National Crime Information Center
items.text: Intrusion reported in FBI crime-records system.

items.name: USDA
items.label: Agriculture Dept. applications
items.text: Taken offline, disrupting tools that support payments to farmers.

graphic.callout: Officials have not linked these incidents.
graphic.note: Other incidents as reported by Nextgov/FCW. Whip illustration.

means.label: Bank deadlines:
means.text: Institutions using FinCEN’s automated filing channel as of Nov. 18 now have until Dec. 30 for reports due Nov. 18 to Dec. 29.

means.label: Still unknown:
means.text: FinCEN hasn’t said what data was accessed or who was responsible. It collects banks’ confidential suspicious activity reports.

means.label: Not linked:
means.text: Officials have not publicly tied FinCEN’s incident to the CIA/ODNI, FBI or USDA intrusions.

sources: Sources: FinCEN notice; ABC News; Nextgov/FCW; The Verge.
